sketches.mechanism: The Maybe monad's >>= (bind) operator silently propagates Nothing through a chain of computations, so once any step yields Nothing, every subsequent step is skipped without error.
sketches.resonance: Grief works like Nothing in a monadic chain — once it enters, every experience that follows passes through without being touched.
sketches.draft:
grief :: Maybe a -> Maybe b -> Maybe c -> Maybe c
grief past present future =
  past >>= const present >>= const future

-- grief (Just 1) (Just 2) (Just 3) => Just 3
-- grief Nothing  (Just 2) (Just 3) => Nothing

sketches.mechanism: In Erlang, a process can link to another process, and when one dies, the linked process also dies unless it traps exits — but trapping exits converts death into a message, not into shared fate.
sketches.resonance: You can survive another's ending only by converting their death into something you merely observe rather than something you share.
sketches.draft:
-module(letting_go).
-export([start/0]).

start() ->
  process_flag(trap_exit, true),
  Pid = spawn_link(fun() -> exit(goodbye) end),
  receive
    {'EXIT', Pid, goodbye} -> alone
  end.

sketches.mechanism: A LEFT JOIN preserves every row from the left table even when no matching row exists on the right, filling the right side with NULL — the absent partner is represented but empty.
sketches.resonance: Memory keeps every moment on the left side intact; what was shared simply fills with NULL where the other person used to be.
sketches.draft:
SELECT
  days.moment,
  together.you
FROM
  days
LEFT JOIN
  together ON days.moment = together.moment;
